name: Júma (Içuã Tupí)
confidence_why: Abrahamson & Abrahamson 1984 and dos Santos 2024, the two first-hand descriptions of Júma, both put main stress on the final syllable of the word (root-final, surfacing as penult on nouns that carry the enclitic =a), against the penult/antepenult rule that StressTyp2 took from Abrahamson 1968 on 'Içuã Tupi', a short early article by the same fieldworker that also calls accent contrastive.
readall_conflicts: No direct conflict, because the one listed work is about Parintintin (Tenharim/Kagwahiva) rather than Júma and states only phrase-level and sentence-level stress. Indirectly, its 'first syllable of the phrase' phrase stress sits uneasily with the word-final primary stress that Abrahamson & Abrahamson 1984 (Os fonemas da língua júma, section 5 Tonicidade, already held by the project in the same our files from the 2026-09-16 pass: 'O acento mais forte recai na última sílaba da palavra', with alternating secondary stresses counted from the right) report for Júma proper, and neither of those matches the catalog's stress on syllable 1 of 2, 2 of 3, 3 of 4, 3 of 5, 4 of 6, 5 of 7 (initial for 2 syllables, penult for 3-4, antepenult for 5+), which is attributed to 'worldwave-2026-08-31-deepnote' with no quote. That catalog record deserves a check against Abrahamson & Abrahamson 1984, but nothing in Pease & Betts 1971 bears on it.

audit.recode_to: Replace the 1968-based 'fixed-dominant, stress on syllable 1 of 2, 2 of 3, 3 of 4, 3 of 5, 4 of 6, 5 of 7 (penult ≤4σ / antepenult ≥5σ), no secondary stress' with a right-edge FINAL / root-final system: dominant set = primary stress on the final syllable of the (root/stem) word with enclitics (=a NMLZ, bound pronouns, postpositions) extrametrical, i.e. final stress over the stress domain, plus alternating secondary stress leftward per A&A 1984 §5A; strict set = morphologically/lexically conditioned (stress-neutral -an and negation circumfix vs stress-attracting -ahim/-uhu/-ʔi/-ʔa; lexical penult set in -ma/-na/-ŋa; final onsetless-V syllables skipped) — cite A&A 1984:§5 (Sér. Ling. 11, pp.157-174) and dos Santos 2024:40-41; domain = word minus enclitics (fixes the not yet coded domain). Keep Abrahamson 1968 Içuã Tupi as a historical note on a possibly distinct, extinct Kawahíva idiolect pair (its speakers' 'tribal name not known', informant killed BY the Júma), and fold the duplicate key name_icuatupi into this row.

sources.citation: Abrahamson, Arne & Joyce Abrahamson. 1984. Os fonemas da língua júma. In R. A. Dooley (ed.), Estudos sobre línguas tupí do Brasil (Série Lingüística 11), 157-174. Brasília: SIL. [SIL Brasil re-typeset online edition, 11 pp; summary by Eunice Burgess of the authors' fuller archived phonemic description; data Sept 1971-Nov 1974 from 7 monolingual adults on igarapé Tapiu, tributary of the rio Içuã, Amazonas]
sources.quote: '5. TONICIDADE. A. O acento duma palavra geralmente recai em sílabas alternadas, recuando a partir da última sílaba. B. O acento mais forte recai na última sílaba da palavra, havendo as seguintes exceções: 1. Quando o padrão silábico V ocorre no final da palavra, o padrão CV que o antecede é que recebe a intensidade do acento [pɛ'yikɔ'pia] ... [pi'rai] 'piranha' ... ['mia'kui]; 2. Quando se acrescente [-an] a uma palavra, o acento da palavra original não muda ['ɔpõ'mãn] > ['ɔpõ'mãnãn]; 3. sources.locator: §5 'Tonicidade', p.10-11 of the online edition (text + page scan verified)
sources.note: Glottolog's top-ranked phonology for Júma, by the same fieldworkers as our 1968 deciding source but on the Júma proper (7 adults, 1971-74); its §5 states FINAL primary stress with alternating secondary stress and morphological/lexical exceptions — contradicts our penult/antepenult count rule and our 'no secondary stress'.

sources.citation: dos Santos, Wesley Nascimento. 2024. Topics on the syntax of Kawahíva: A Tupí-Guaraní language from the Brazilian Amazon. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. xvi+233 pp. (eScholarship 7n3020c1). Phonology based on first-hand fieldwork with the Juma (3 speakers) and Jupaú.
sources.quote: p.37: oral/nasal vowel contrast 'appears to be restricted to the root-final syllable, which coincides with the location of stress.' p.40: 'Stress is assigned to the root-final syllable of a word. ... In nouns, this stress pattern is a bit obscured as they always surface with the extrametrical nominalizing enclitic =a. On the surface, then, stress falls on the penultimate syllable of nouns bearing the enclitic =a.' exx. sources.locator: ch.3 §3.2.1 'Sound inventory, phonotactics and stress', printed pp.37, 40-41 (extracted text)
sources.note: Only modern first-hand description of Juma (and Jupaú) phonology; §3.2.1 pp.40-41 states root-final stress, extrametrical nominalizer =a, stress-attracting vs stress-neutral suffixes — contradicts the count-based coding and supplies the morphological conditioning the record lacks (domain currently not yet coded).
